subject: radiology
title: Genitourinary radiology: key investigations and classic signs

steps.tx: Choosing the right test is the core of genitourinary imaging. **Non-contrast CT** is the investigation of choice for renal and ureteric stones, because nearly all calculi show up, even radiolucent ones. **Ultrasound** is the most common initial test for urinary obstruction, hydronephrosis and pyonephrosis, and is also the usual first look at urinary tract malignancy. Remember these pairings, as they recur in NEET-PG and INI-CET questions.

steps.tx: Voiding studies answer the paediatric and reflux questions. The **micturating cystourethrogram (MCU)** is the investigation of choice for **vesicoureteral reflux** and **posterior urethral valves**, and it is the best method to see the posterior urethra. Retrograde urethrography is reserved for the anterior, penile urethra. In a suspected valve, look for a dilated posterior urethra on the voiding film.

left.title: Voiding (MCU)
points: Investigation of choice for posterior urethral valves

steps.tx: Several IVU signs point to a specific diagnosis. A **cobra head** or adder head appearance, a bulbous distal ureter inside the opacified bladder, indicates a **ureterocoele**. A **drooping lily** appearance of the distal ureter is typical of an ectopic ureter. In polycystic kidney disease, calyces stretched over cysts give the **spider leg** appearance, and the **Swiss cheese** nephrogram reflects innumerable lucent cysts.

steps.tx: Some signs point to chronic scarring or stones. A **rim sign** of thinned parenchyma around a dilated pelvicalyceal system suggests **chronic hydronephrosis**. **Papillary necrosis** shows an egg-in-cup or ring sign, while **medullary sponge kidney** shows a paint brush appearance. A **staghorn calculus** fills the renal pelvis and extends into the calyces, and it is typically a struvite stone with infection.

vis.alt: A medical image (CT or X-ray) showing a large, branched staghorn calculus filling the renal pelvis and extending into the calyces of a kidney.
vis.caption: Staghorn calculus: filling renal pelvis and calyces. Image: Nevit Dilmen ( talk ), CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons.

steps.tx: Renal masses are graded with the **Bosniak classification** on contrast CT. Simple cysts are Bosniak I and need no follow-up. Higher categories have increasing thickened or enhancing septa and solid components, and category IV carries a high malignancy risk. Renal artery stenosis is the classic cause of renovascular hypertension, and the **string of beads** appearance of the renal artery reflects medial fibroplasia. CT angiography is the next most accurate screen after catheter angiography, which remains the gold standard.

steps.tx: Uterine and scrotal imaging complete the picture. **Hysterosalpingography** shows the uterine cavity but cannot assess the outer uterine contour, so it cannot reliably separate a bicornuate from a septate uterus. A **didelphys** uterus has two separate horns and cervices, while a **unicornuate** uterus gives a banana-shaped cavity. For **torsion of the testis**, colour Doppler ultrasound is the imaging of choice, showing reduced or absent flow.
